subject: Silverpine: request for SLO carveout + commercial concession
messages:
From: Cathy Zhou <cathy@silverpine.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@silverpine.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production SLO ask + commercial question

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to finalizing the SOW but two items came up from our engineering and procurement teams that are blockers for signature:

1) Uptime SLO: our ingestion pipeline is very spiky for batch windows. We’d like the contract to reflect 99.9% uptime for the batch inference endpoint (instead of the standard 99.95% across the board). We understand this is non-standard and are willing to take a more conservative credit ladder.

2) Latency SLO carveout: for calls that include >8k token context (historical aggregation), we need p95 latency at 1.2s instead of 500ms. This is only for a named endpoint used for nightly enrichment.

From procurement: if Redwood can accept these terms and provide a 15% implementation credit (applied to the first 3 months of committed usage) we can sign within two weeks. I’ve attached the SOW and a short trace bundle from our QA run.

Could you loop in deal desk/legal? We’re happy to be explicit about the scope (endpoint name + traffic profile).

—Cathy
Cathy Zhou
Head of Platform Engineering
Silverpine Analytics

Attachment: Silverpine_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
Attachment: Latency_Trace_20270504.zip (zip, 8MB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Cathy Zhou <cathy@silverpine.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production SLO ask + commercial question

Cathy —

Appreciate the clear ask and the traces, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front:
- We can scope a named endpoint with a different uptime SLO (batch-infer.silverpine.prod).
- We can also carve out a higher p95 for the >8k-token path, scoped to that endpoint and flagged in the routing policy.

I’m looping in Marissa (deal desk) and Jonas (VP sales) to get commercial and exec alignment. Marissa — can you put together the standard concession language you’ve used for similar batch carveouts and a recommended service credit ladder? If we need exec signoff, Jonas can weigh in.

Cathy — I’ll follow up with an ops-runbook suggestion (fallback variants + cache policy) to reduce our exposure.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

> On 2027-05-02, Cathy wrote:
> > We’re close to finalizing the SOW but two items came up ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T11:31:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production SLO ask + commercial question

Team —

Draft concession language below. I’ve kept it conditional on a 6-month committed usage minimum (to offset operational overhead) and added a hybrid credit structure so we’re not overly exposed if batch windows spike. Please review — I need exec + legal approval to move to procurement.

Key commercial terms (proposal):
- Endpoint scoping: carveout applies only to endpoint id "batch-infer.silverpine.prod" and any downstream replicas listed in SOW appendix A.
- Uptime: 99.90% monthly uptime target for the named endpoint only. Standard 99.95% remains for all other RTX endpoints.
- Remedies: If monthly uptime falls below 99.90% for the named endpoint, Redwood will issue a service credit as follows: 1.0% credit for each 0.1% below target, capped at 10% of monthly invoice for that endpoint.
- Latency carveout: For requests where context length >8000 tokens, p95 target is 1.2s. If p95 exceeds 1.2s, Redwood will provide a per-incident credit of 0.2% up to 2% in a given month for latency incidents (separate from uptime credits).
- Committed credit: Redwood will provide a one-time implementation credit equal to 15% of the first 3 months' committed usage if Silverpine signs a 6-month committed plan.
- Operational conditions: carveout applies only when traffic matches the attached trace profile (nightly window 02:00-05:00 PST) and the customer agrees to enable Redwood’s prefix caching and fallback to quantized variant during those windows.

Asks for approval:
- Jonas: Exec signoff for the 15% implementation credit (this is outside standard authority).
- Lauren/Legal: sign off on separate latency-incident credit ladder and the endpoint-scoping language (we must ensure this does not create a global precedence).

I’ve attached precedent language used for a prior carveout (anonymized) and marked where we deviate.

—Marissa
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: precedent_carveout_redlines.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

> On 2027-05-03, Ben wrote:
> > I’m looping in Marissa and Jonas ...

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-07T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production SLO ask + commercial question

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. I’m OK to authorize the 15% implementation credit provided the following limits are enforced:
1) The service credit cap and per-incident latency cap remain as you wrote (we should tighten language to prevent stacking; latency-incident credits must be mutually exclusive of uptime credits for the same time window).
2) We add an emergency throttle clause: if the batch window causes sustained degraded performance on multi-tenant pools, Redwood can invoke short-term rate-limiting (documented with an ops runbook) and Silverpine agrees to coordinate a traffic shift.
3) Approval is conditional on a signed 6-month committed usage amendment (minimum spend $60K/month).

I want Lauren to confirm the non-precedent language — this is a carveout narrowly scoped to a single endpoint and traffic pattern. Marissa: get legal redlines and update the SOW appendix with endpoint IDs and the traffic fingerprint.

If Lauren signs off, I’ll email Exec approval to seal the commercial concession.

—Jonas
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

> On 2027-05-05, Marissa wrote:
> > Draft concession language below ...

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production SLO ask + commercial question — legal redlines

Jonas/Marissa —

Legal has reviewed. Key edits below (high level):
- Precedence: Insert explicit clause that language applies only to the SOW and is not to be used as precedent for other customers.
- Off-ramps: Insert operational off-ramp — if batch traffic increases beyond the agreed fingerprint and causes platform-wide severity, Redwood may require migration to a dedicated pool; customer will be charged at list price for dedicated capacity after a 14-day remediation window.
- Stacking: Clarified that uptime and latency credits are mutually exclusive for overlapping events; also clarified measurement method (server-side p95 computed over successful requests).
- Documentation: Require Silverpine to sign an appendix which lists endpoint IDs and weekly rolling traffic histograms for the first 12 weeks; failure to provide these will void the carveout.

With those edits, legal is willing to approve the non-standard SLO carveout and the 15% implementation credit. Jonas, please confirm exec approval and I’ll produce the redline SOW for countersignature.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

> On 2027-05-07, Jonas wrote:
> > I’m OK to authorize the 15% implementation credit provided the following limits ...
